behaviour-switch.answer: The switch is DialectBehavior.CompileTimeArithmeticImplementorDefined (src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Control/DialectBehavior.cs:301): before 2023 compile-time arithmetic expressions use standard arithmetic (§2002:7.2.5.2 GR1 'Standard arithmetic shall be used for all arithmetic operations'), and such expressions occur only in DEFINE and EVALUATE directives, constant conditional expressions and constant entries (§2002:7.2.5); its only call sites are the >>DEFINE/>>IF/>>EVALUATE evaluator and the constant-entry binder (git grep CompileTimeArithmetic in src). This directive's format carries only keywords or comment-text, no compile-time arithmetic expression, so the switch cannot reach the rule; >>PAGE takes only comment-text, which 'is not checked syntactically' (§2002:7.2.16.2 SR2), so digits or operators in it are never evaluated. At --std 2002 comment-text has no effect: page-junk.cob (re-run this session: ONE, TWO, with COPY NOSUCH., unbalanced quotes and +-*/ in comment-text) and pb1352_directive_lines_not_replaced (matches its .out at 2002).
